pictures.scene: Jozef Israëls, 'Alleen op de wereld' — the old man left sitting alone by the empty bed with his head in his hand, a Maskil of Asaph, why have You rejected us forever O God
pictures.name: pd_israels_alleen_op_de_wereld

pictures.scene: Balthasar Paul Ommeganck, Landschap met schapen en een hooiwagen — the flock lying down in the open pasture with the hay cart behind them, why does Your anger smolder against the sheep of Your pasture
pictures.name: pd_ommeganck_schapen_hooiwagen

pictures.scene: Alphonse Mucha, Kázání mistra Jana Husa v kapli Betlémské — the whole congregation packed into the chapel to hear the preaching, remember Your congregation which You purchased long ago
pictures.name: pd_mucha_kazani_husa_betlemske

pictures.scene: Théodore Frère, Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives — the city lying along its ridge seen across the valley in the evening light, and redeemed as the tribe of Your inheritance, Mount Zion where You dwell
pictures.name: pd_frere_jerusalem_mount_of_olives

pictures.scene: Louis Daguerre, The Ruins of Holyrood Chapel — the roofless chapel with its windows open to the sky and the floor full of rubble, turn Your steps to the everlasting ruins, to everything in the sanctuary the enemy has destroyed
pictures.name: pd_daguerre_holyrood_chapel_ruins

pictures.scene: Hendrick Cornelisz Vroom, Battle of Haarlemmermeer — the ships crowded together on the water with their flags and pennants run up, Your foes have roared within Your meeting place, they have unfurled their banners as signs
pictures.name: pd_vroom_haarlemmermeer

pictures.scene: Hubert Robert, Démolition de l'Eglise Saint-Jean-en-Grève — the workmen up on the walls of the church swinging at the stonework and pulling it down, like men wielding axes in a thicket of trees and smashing all the carvings with hatchets and picks
pictures.name: pd_robert_demolition_saint_jean

pictures.scene: Jan Abrahamsz Beerstraaten, De puinhopen van het Oude Stadhuis te Amsterdam na de brand van 7 juli 1652 — the burnt-out shell of the great building still smoking in the snow, they have burned Your sanctuary to the ground, they have defiled the dwelling place of Your Name
pictures.name: pd_beerstraaten_puinhopen_stadhuis

pictures.scene: Alfred Wierusz-Kowalski, Wilki w nocy — the wolves coming on together over the snow in the dark, they said in their hearts, we will crush them completely
pictures.name: pd_wierusz_kowalski_wilki_w_nocy

pictures.scene: Aert van der Neer, Nocturnal Fire in a Dutch City — the whole town lit up by the fire burning through it at night, they burned down every place where God met us in the land
pictures.name: pd_van_der_neer_nocturnal_fire

pictures.scene: Philips Koninck, Rivierlandschap — the enormous flat country under an empty sky with nothing standing up in it, there are no signs for us to see, there is no longer any prophet
pictures.name: pd_koninck_rivierlandschap

pictures.scene: Isidor Kaufmann, The Kabbalist — the old scholar sitting still over his book waiting on an answer, and none of us knows how long this will last, how long O God will the enemy taunt You
pictures.name: pd_kaufmann_the_kabbalist

pictures.scene: Hieronymus Bosch, Kruisdraging — the jeering faces pressed in around Christ on the road, will the foe revile Your name forever, why do You withdraw Your strong right hand
pictures.name: pd_bosch_kruisdraging

pictures.scene: Markus Pernhart, Großglockner von der Hohenwartscharte — the great peak and its glacier standing up out of the cloud, stretch it out to destroy them, yet God is my King from ancient times
pictures.name: pd_pernhart_grossglockner

pictures.scene: Louis Meijer, Storm in het Nauw van Calais — the sea heaped up and split open under the ships in the gale, working salvation on the earth, You divided the sea by Your strength
pictures.name: pd_meijer_storm_nauw_van_calais

pictures.scene: Andrea Vaccaro, Tobias and the Fish — the great fish dragged up out of the river and held down on the bank, You smashed the heads of the dragons of the sea, You crushed the heads of Leviathan
pictures.name: pd_vaccaro_tobias_and_the_fish

pictures.scene: Jan Asselijn, De doorbraak van de Sint-Anthonisdijk bij Amsterdam — the dike burst open and the water pouring through the gap across the land, You fed him to the creatures of the desert, You broke open the fountain and the flood
pictures.name: pd_asselijn_doorbraak_sint_anthonisdijk

pictures.scene: Eugen Bracht, Rast in der Syrischen Wüste — the dry bed and the burnt sand of the desert with the travellers halted on it, You dried up the ever-flowing rivers, the day is Yours and also the night
pictures.name: pd_bracht_rast_in_der_syrischen_wueste

pictures.scene: Herman van Swanevelt, Italiaans landschap — the two men under the great tree looking out over the plain to the far horizon, You established the moon and the sun, You set all the boundaries of the earth
pictures.name: pd_swanevelt_italiaans_landschap

pictures.scene: Charles Leickert, Stadsgezicht in de winter — the snow lying on the roofs of the town and the smoke going up from the chimneys, You made the summer and winter, remember how the enemy has mocked You O LORD
pictures.name: pd_leickert_stadsgezicht_in_de_winter

pictures.scene: John Everett Millais, The Return of the Dove to the Ark — the girls holding the dove safe in their hands with the olive sprig still in its beak, how a foolish people has spurned Your name, do not deliver the soul of Your dove to beasts
pictures.name: pd_millais_return_of_the_dove_to_the_ark

pictures.scene: Ludwig Knaus, Kartoffelernte — the poor family out in the field gathering the potatoes with the baby carried among them, do not forget the lives of Your afflicted forever, consider Your covenant
pictures.name: pd_knaus_kartoffelernte

pictures.scene: Sebastiaan Vrancx, Plundering van een gehucht — the armed men riding into the hamlet and taking it apart, for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the land, do not let the oppressed retreat in shame
pictures.name: pd_vrancx_plundering_van_een_gehucht

pictures.scene: Gerard van Nijmegen, Berglandschap bij Düsseldorf — the woman in the red skirt with her small child beside the ox cart on the timber bridge, may the poor and needy praise Your name, rise up O God defend Your cause
pictures.name: pd_van_nijmegen_berglandschap_bij_dusseldorf

pictures.scene: Cornelis Dusart, Herberg met boeren — the grinning man with his glass up and the whole inn yard loud behind him, remember how the fool mocks You all day long, do not disregard the clamor of Your adversaries
pictures.name: pd_dusart_herberg_met_boeren

pictures.scene: Jan Martszen de Jonge, Ruitergevecht — the riders crashing into each other with the sword up and the horses screaming, the uproar of Your enemies that ascends continually
pictures.name: pd_martszen_ruitergevecht

lines.text: A Maskil of Asaph.
Why have You rejected us forever, O God?
Why does Your anger smolder
against the sheep of Your pasture?
Remember Your congregation,
which You purchased long ago
and redeemed as the tribe of Your inheritance—
Mount Zion, where You dwell.
Turn Your steps to the everlasting ruins,
to everything in the sanctuary the enemy has destroyed.
Your foes have roared within Your meeting place;
they have unfurled their banners as signs,
like men wielding axes in a thicket of trees
and smashing all the carvings with hatchets and picks.
They have burned Your sanctuary to the ground;
they have defiled the dwelling place of Your Name.
They said in their hearts,
“We will crush them completely.”
They burned down every place
where God met us in the land.
There are no signs for us to see.
There is no longer any prophet.
And none of us knows how long this will last.
How long, O God, will the enemy taunt You?
Will the foe revile Your name forever?
Why do You withdraw Your strong right hand?
Stretch it out to destroy them!
Yet God is my King from ancient times,
working salvation on the earth.
You divided the sea by Your strength;
You smashed the heads of the dragons of the sea;
You crushed the heads of Leviathan;
You fed him to the creatures of the desert.
You broke open the fountain and the flood;
You dried up the ever-flowing rivers.
The day is Yours, and also the night;
You established the moon and the sun.
You set all the boundaries of the earth;
You made the summer and winter.
Remember how the enemy has mocked You, O LORD,
how a foolish people has spurned Your name.
Do not deliver the soul of Your dove to beasts;
do not forget the lives of Your afflicted forever.
Consider Your covenant,
for haunts of violence fill the dark places of the land.
Do not let the oppressed retreat in shame;
may the poor and needy praise Your name.
Rise up, O God; defend Your cause!
Remember how the fool mocks You all day long.
Do not disregard the clamor of Your adversaries,
the uproar of Your enemies that ascends continually.
